review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–76) and found no justified finding. The only repeated pieces are small. Both `lucas_primality` and `reverse_lucas_primality` use `orderOf_injective (Units.coeHom _) Units.val_injective` to move between `orderOf a` and `orderOf a'` for a unit. That is a one-line call to an existing lemma, so a shared helper would be a thin wrapper. Both also use `p - 1 > 0` from `1 < p`, which is routine. `lucas_primality_iff` just combines the two theorems. The two proofs run in opposite directions: one builds the unit from `a`, the other takes the unit's coercion. Because of that, they share no non-trivial block that could be factored into a lemma. I did not search other files for duplicates, since the rubric concerns repetition inside proofs.
